full_judgment:
Mr. Abdus Salam Mamun, J. :-This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the impugned Judgment and decree dated 29.10.2.000 passed by the Sub-ordinate Judge, First Court, Laxmipur in Title Appeal No. 59 of 1997 affirming the judgment and decree dated 29.3.1997 passed by the Senior Assistant Judge, Laxmipur in Title Suit No.. 68 of_1995 should not be set aside. 

 2. Facts of the case, in brief, are that one Lakiatullah, the predecessor of both the Plaintiffs and the Defendant No. I instituted the Title Suit No. 68 of 1995 against his son Mominullah and two grand-sons, one represented by his father being minor, praying for a decree declaring that the Reba-bil-Ewaj deed No. 707 dated 22.2.1995 alleged to be executed by him in the Chandraganj Sub-registry office was forged, manufactured, without consideration, void and not acted upon stating inter alia, that the plaintiff was an old man of 90/95 years of age and was the owner and possessor of 1.37 acres of land mentioned in the schedule to the plaint by way of his inheritance as well as purchase. He had his dwelling house on the land under Mouza 63 Banchanagar and that he did not make any Heba-bil-Ewaj deed in favour of his son and grand-sons on 22.2.1995 transferring his entire property in their favour depriving his daughters and the said Heba-bil-Ewaj deed N0.707 dated 22.2.1995 registered in the Chandraganj Sub-registry Office was forged and fabricated and not acted upon and was thus void. In fact, his son, the Defendant No. 1, whom he earlier separated being disappointed, approached him in the later part of Magh, 1401 Bangla for Tk.20,000/- to send his grand-son, the Defendant No. 2, to abroad being he was in shortage of money and on good faith and considering the future of the defendant No.2, he agreed to give Tk.20,000/- to his grand-son for his going abroad and also agreed to collect that amount of Tk. 20,000 by selling out .20 decimals of char-land from char Ramani Mohon Mouza and asked the Defendant No. 1, his son, to find out a buyer and 10/12 days later, the Defendant No. I came with some other persons and obtained his thumb impression saying that he arranged sale of .20 decimals of char-land for Tk.18,000/- to those people and received the money and on good faith, the plaintiff put his thumb impression on the said deed without knowing its contents. But subsequently, he came to learn that his son, the defendant No. 1, has, fraudulently taken away his entire property i-e, 1.37 acres of land by a Heba-bil-Ewaj deed in collusion with the employees of the Sub-registry office which, he never intended to give to the Defendants No. 1 or 2 or 3 alone by depriving his three daughters, one of whom was living with him in his dwelling house being divorced. The said Heba-bil-Ewaj deed was forged and fraudulently obtained and void. 

 3. The Defendants No. 1-3 entered appearance in the suit by filing written statements making only denials of the statements made in the plaint. During the pendency of the suit and before peremptory hearing of it, the plaintiff Lakiatullah died and his three daughters were substituted as Plaintiffs in his place. These substituted Plaintiffs thereafter made an application for amendment of the plaint on 26.11.1996 and by way of amendment brought into the suit a new cause, to the effect that Lakiatullah executed a deed of gift on 12.3.1995 in their favour and giving them .82 decimals of land out of the schedule under a registered Heba-nama No.2622 which their father inadvertently did not mention in the plaint alleging further, that their brother has forged the alleged deed of Heba-bil-Ewaj. The Defendants, on the other hand, also submitted an additional written statements on 3.10.1996 taking a new defence in respect of possession of the suit land claiming their exclusive possession and making out reasons for gift to the plaintiff etc. The learned trial Court, after conclusion of trial, was pleased to dismiss the suit holding amongst others that the plaintiffs could not prove exclusive possessions in the suit land and that the Defendant No. 1 is dwelling in the suit land having his homestead and one of the plaintiffs is living in west Banchanagar and the other in Laxmipur and that the deed of gift was properly registered and that the Plaintiffs late father Lakiatullah himself admitted execution of the disputed deed by stating that he put his thumb impression on a deed. The Plaintiffs failed to prove that the Defendants got the registered deed in question by way of false personation. The learned trial Court thus held that the suit was not maintainable. The plaintiffs thereafter, preferred an appeal before the District Judge, Laxmipur being the Title Appeal No.59 of 1977 which was ultimately heard and disposed of by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge, 1st Court, Laxmipur who was pleased to disallow the appeal and affirm the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court holding that the deed in question was executed by the plaintiff Lakiatullah himself and for the first time the plaintiffs disclosed about having a Heba Deed No. 2622 of 1995 by way of amendment of the plaint after substitution on the demise of the plaintiff Lakiatullah. But Lakiatullah did not mention this Heba deed in his plaint and that the jurisdiction of the Chandraganj Sub-registry office and the Laxmipur Sub-registry office was common jurisdiction and that the Title Suit No.68 of 1995 was not maintainable, for, the plaintiffs-appellants had no right, title or locus standi in the suit land. They were not entitled to be substituted and the appeal is also not maintainable. 

 4. The Plaintiffs- appellants have preferred this application under Section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure on the grounds amongst others that the-Courts below since found joint possession in the suit land ought to have decreed the suit. 

 6. Mr. Mihir Kanti Majumder, the Learned Advocate, appearing for the Opposite Party submitted that the findings of both the. Courts below, in respect of execution of the Heba deed in question by Lakiatullah in favour of the defendants are concurrent and thus the appellate Court has rightly affirmed the, judgment and decree of the trial Court and held that the jurisdiction of both the sub-registry offices were common. The Plaintiff could not prove their case by adducing sufficient evidence that the Heba-bil-Ewaj deed in question was forged and as such, the suit was rightly dismissed and appeal allowed. 

 11. But in the instant case, both the substituted plaintiffs and the defendants have committed illegalities by making additional cause, so far it related to the deed of gift No. 2622 of 1995 in favour of the plaintiffs, allegedly made by Lakiatullah and also by raising additional defence by the defendants by way of filing additional written statements in the suit after death of the Plaintiff in respect of possession of the suit land and circumstances leading to the gift. Both the Courts below have erred in law in entertaining and adjudicating the additional cause and defence respectively and their judgments and decrees are perversed in law. 

 It therefore appears that the Courts below instead of appreciation of evidence on record and assessment of it from legal perspectives and without considering the law applicable  in this case, have traveled beyond the record and both the judgments and decrees are thus bad in law. They are, therefore, liable to be set aside. 

 The impugned judgment and decree dated 29.10.2000 passed by' the Sub-ordinate ' Judge, First Court, Laxmipur, in Title Appeal. No. 59 of 1997 affirming the: judgment and decree dated 29.3.1997 passed by the Senior Assistant Judge, Laxmipur in Title Suit No. 68 of 1995 is set aside.
